original_statement: Effects are reviewed; materializations are signed; the client re-derives the materialization and refuses on mismatch. This check lives in the module core and cannot be disabled
restatement: Given a reviewed effect, the module core must independently re-derive the materialization and refuse to sign whenever it disagrees with the driver-supplied one, and this check must be unconditional: (s1) the client independently computes what the materialization should be, without trusting the driver's copy; (s2) if the driver-supplied materialization differs from the client's independent derivation in any way, the client refuses to sign; (s3) this check cannot be bypassed by any configuration flag, plugin, or user preference.

restatement_clauses.text: Given a reviewed effect, the client independently computes what the materialization should be, without trusting the driver's copy.
If the driver-supplied materialization differs from the client's independent derivation in any way, the client refuses to sign.
This check cannot be bypassed by any configuration flag, plugin, or user preference — it is unconditional module-core behavior.

goal: A module-core check that independently re-derives the materialization from the reviewed effect, refuses to sign on any mismatch, and cannot be bypassed by configuration, plugin, or user preference.
acceptance_criteria: Given a reviewed effect, the client independently computes what the materialization should be, without trusting the driver's copy.

This check cannot be bypassed by any configuration flag, plugin, or user preference — it is unconditional module-core behavior.

acceptance_tests.proves: The client's independent-derivation path is real and actually reproduces the driver's own honestly-computed materialization — not stubbed to always match without doing the work.
acceptance_tests.description: Given a reviewed effect, the client independently computes what the materialization should be, without trusting the driver's copy.

acceptance_tests.proves: Not just 'does it accept the good case' but 'does it reject every bad case' — a materialization tampered in any single field, across many random trials, is always refused.
acceptance_tests.description: If the driver-supplied materialization differs from the client's independent derivation in any way, the client refuses to sign.

acceptance_tests.proves: Every reachable configuration state (toggling one setting/plugin/flag at a time from the default) still refuses a mismatched materialization — a config surface that quietly suppresses the check anywhere in that reachable space is caught as a counterexample.
acceptance_tests.description: This check cannot be bypassed by any configuration flag, plugin, or user preference — it is unconditional module-core behavior.
